title: Texas schools after the 2026 election
slideTitles: An appointed commissioner enforces school law.
Two schools could cost Austin its elected board.
Both parties already vote for school funding.
Most likely, two schools close and the board stays.
5 pending decisions will settle what changes.

states.lead: Democrats won 4 statewide offices.
states.body: The winners have yet to take office.

states.lead: Democrats won a House majority.
states.body: The final House seat count is pending.

states.lead: Republicans kept the Senate.
states.body: 19 Republican and 12 Democratic seats are expected next session.

states.lead: The education-board majority depends on District 8.
states.body: A Democratic win there would give the party 8 seats. A recount is possible.

states.lead: The Legislature writes school law.
states.body: The House and Senate also decide state school funding.

states.lead: The governor appoints the education commissioner.
states.body: The Senate must confirm the appointment.

states.lead: The commissioner decides how the state intervenes.
states.body: State law sets the conditions for replacing elected trustees with an appointed board.

states.lead: 102 open campuses have a rating.
states.body: The count excludes closed campuses and programs without a letter grade.

states.lead: The appeals could prevent board replacement.
states.body: Their final ratings and counted years remain pending.

states.lead: The elected board could be replaced.
states.body: Parents at both schools petitioned to close them instead.

states.lead: The incumbent can still nominate a commissioner.
states.body: The governor-elect takes office at inauguration.

states.lead: Petitions are due before the governor's inauguration.
states.body: They ask the state to close both schools. The superintendent validates them first.

states.lead: Successful appeals could prevent board replacement.
states.body: Final ratings are scheduled for Dec 11.

states.lead: Trustees can request closure or appointed managers.
states.body: The request needs approval at a public board meeting.

states.lead: The new governor can nominate a commissioner.
states.body: The nominee needs Senate confirmation.

states.lead: Who signs the February order?
states.body: With valid petitions, that order would close both schools rather than replace the board.

states.lead: Republicans are expected to keep their majority.
states.body: The confirmation threshold assumes all 31 senators attend.

states.lead: A nominee would need both parties' votes.
states.body: That assumes all 31 attend and all 12 Democrats support the nominee.

states.lead: Mike Morath serves until a successor qualifies.
states.body: Lawful removal or another applicable vacancy rule could alter his tenure.

states.lead: Senators can change their chamber rules.
states.body: The lieutenant governor's committee and agenda powers depend on rules senators can revise.

states.lead: HB 2 added $8.5B for public schools.
states.body: It pays for teacher pay and special education in the 2026–27 state budget.

states.lead: Every senator voted yes, 31 to 0.
states.body: That session also passed vouchers. Abbott and Patrick, who set its agenda, have now lost.

states.lead: Austin ISD still had to cut its budget.
states.body: It faced a $181M gap before 2026–27 cuts and budgeted $715.5M in property taxes for the state in 2025–26.

states.lead: Valid petitions would close Burnet and Webb.
states.body: Initial counts topped the required majority. TEA is reviewing a complaint about signatures.

states.lead: If petitions fail, a state board takes over.
states.body: Morath may appoint it. Once confirmed, her commissioner can replace every manager.

states.lead: Hinojosa's TEA would run a different takeover.
states.body: She pledged to end state takeovers. Morath's TEA has run Houston's since 2023.

states.lead: Each decision names who makes it.
states.body: Some have legal deadlines. Others wait on a vote by elected officials.

states.lead: Trustees must meet before the request deadline.
states.body: Trustees need a public vote to request a different intervention.
